Adult (6-month-old) control C57BL6 wild-type mice and transgenic AD mice were used. Transgenic APP_SweDI (expressing amyloid precursor protein (APP)) harboring the Swedish K670N/M671L, Dutch E693Q, and Iowa D694N mutations; C57BL/6-Tg (Thy1-APPSwDutIowa, BWevn/Mmjax) mice were used as reported previously by us [27]. These mice produce Aβ plaques at an age >6 months. Mice were sacrificed by decapitation, the cortex dissected and collected in tubes. The cortex was homogenized in 1 ml phosphate buffered saline (PBS) with a protease inhibitor cocktail (Sigma-Aldrich, P-8340) by sonication. This solution was centrifuged at 14,000xg for 20 min at 4°C and the supernatant was collected. Total protein amount was detected with Bradford assay with Coomassie brilliant blue G250 dye (Bio-Rad, #1610406).

Native Western Blots were performed as described previously [26]. Proteins (25 µl) were loaded on to the 10% Bis-Tris polyacrylamide gel (Invitrogen, NP0301BOX) with 5 μl of sample buffer. Electrophoresis was performed under native conditions for 30-40 min (tau) or 25 min (Aβ) at 200 V. Samples were electrotransferred onto PVDF membranes for 20 min at 25 V in semi-dry transfer cell (Thermo Scientific). Blotting was done with the WesternBreeze Chemiluminescent immunodetection system (Invitrogen). Blots were blocked for 30 min and incubated overnight on a shaker at 4°C with primary antibodies against tau (Tau-5, ThermoFisher Scientific, AHB0042, 1:1000) or human Aβ42) (BioLegend, SIG-39399, clone 6E10, 1:1000). Blots were incubated with alkaline phosphatase-conjugated secondary antibody (anti-mouse) for 30 min at room temperature. Following brief washing steps, blots were incubated in CDP-Star chemiluminescent substrate solution (Roche) for 15 min and visualized with a cooled CCD camera (SearchLight, ThermoFisher Scientific). A multi-colored molecular weight marker (Invitrogen, LC5800) was run as a control (Fig. 2A).Fig. 2Combined Western Blot and agarose gel elution (WANGEL). (A) A colored molecular weight marker was loaded on a Western Blot gel and (B) full length tau (FLT tau) was detected on a Western Blot with a size of 60 kDa using the tau-5 antibody. (C) Tau protein was loaded on Western Blot gels incuding colored molecular weight markers and (D) the bands of interest (arrow) were cut out of the gel. (E) In order to elute tau on agarose gels, a tube was prepared with 4% agarose at the top, followed by 1% agarose with the cut bands embedded and loading buffer, then the collection buffer was added and the tube was closed with a 3 µm membrane insert. Western Blots are a gold standard approach when it comes to detecting different molecular weight species [21]. Proteins are usually separated on native or denatured polyacrylamide gels (PAGE) and detected using an antibody-enzyme system (e.g. enhanced chemiluminescence). Using Western Blots, it is acknowledged that full length tau is a 60 kDa protein and Aβ(42) and Aβ(40) are small 4 kDa peptides. The Aβ(42) peptides can aggregate and show a smear of higher molecular weight species. In addition, tau is present as smaller tau fragments in CSF [22]. Furthermore, post-analysis of Western Blot eluates through ELISA or mass spectrometry is limited owing to the toxic properties of polyacrylamide.

steps.title: Prepare 1 % agarose gel
steps.instruction: Weigh agarose (Sigma‑Aldrich, catalog A9539) to obtain a 1 % (w/v) solution, heat in a microwave at 800 W for 1 min, pour into the gel chamber, insert a 10‑lane comb in the middle, and allow to cool and solidify.

steps.title: Prepare electrophoresis buffer
steps.instruction: Make running buffer containing 100 mM MES (Roth, catalog 4256.2) and 100 mM histidine (Roth, catalog 1696.1), adjust pH to 6.1.

steps.title: Load samples onto agarose gel
steps.instruction: Mix each sample with bromophenol‑blue/glycerine loading buffer (25 µl per lane) and load into the wells of the 1 % agarose gel.

steps.title: Run agarose electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Run the gel at 100 V, 250 mA, 40 W for up to 90 min (or until the desired migration is achieved).

steps.title: Stain agarose gel
steps.instruction: Stain the gel with PageBlue protein staining solution (ThermoFisher Scientific, catalog 24620) according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Excise bands of interest
steps.instruction: Using a clean scalpel, cut out the bands corresponding to the target proteins/peptides (size range 0–80 kDa).

steps.title: Optional: Gel‑extraction kit elution
steps.instruction: Process the excised bands with the QuikPik gel extraction kit (Stratagene, catalog 400855) and electro‑elute against the cathode/anode for 60 min.

steps.title: Prepare agarose extraction tubes
steps.instruction: For each sample, use a 2.5 ml PE vial (Roth, catalog 5863.1). Pipette 1 ml of 4 % agarose into the bottom, let it cool and solidify.

substeps.instruction: Place the excised PAGE band(s) onto the hardened 4 % agarose.
Pipette 1 ml of hand‑warm 1 % agarose over the band, allow to cool and solidify.

steps.title: Assemble tube for elution
steps.instruction: Cut off the bottom of the vial, seal the opening with a Millicell culture insert (3 µm pore size, 12 mm, Merck, catalog PITP01250).

substeps.instruction: Using a syringe, add 1 ml of the MES/histidine running buffer (same composition as step 2) into the tube.
Add 10 µl of bromophenol‑blue buffer to the tube to aid visualization of the elution front.

steps.title: Elute proteins/peptides in agarose chamber
steps.instruction: Place the assembled tubes into the horizontal agarose electrophoresis chamber and run at 100 V for 20–60 min (direction cathode or anode as required for the target molecule).

steps.title: Collect elution buffer
steps.instruction: After electrophoresis, retrieve the buffer from each tube; this contains the eluted protein or peptide.

steps.title: Prepare mouse cortical extracts (if applicable)
steps.instruction: Dissect cortex from 6‑month‑old C57BL/6 or APP_SweDI mice, homogenize in 1 ml PBS containing protease inhibitor cocktail (Sigma‑Aldrich, catalog P‑8340) by sonication, centrifuge at 14 000 × g for 20 min at 4 °C, collect supernatant, and determine protein concentration with Bradford assay using Coomassie brilliant blue G‑250 dye (Bio‑Rad, catalog #1610406).

steps.title: Native PAGE (Western blot) separation
steps.instruction: Load 25 µl of each protein sample (with 5 µl native sample buffer) onto a 10 % Bis‑Tris polyacrylamide gel (Invitrogen, catalog NP0301BOX). Run under native conditions at 200 V for 30–40 min for tau or 25 min for Aβ.

steps.title: Transfer and immunodetection (optional verification)
steps.instruction: Electro‑transfer proteins to a PVDF membrane in a semi‑dry transfer cell (Thermo Scientific) at 25 V for 20 min. Block membrane 30 min, incubate overnight at 4 °C with primary antibody (tau‑5, ThermoFisher, catalog AHB0042, 1:1000; or Aβ42, BioLegend SIG‑39399 clone 6E10, 1:1000). Incubate with alkaline phosphatase‑conjugated anti‑mouse secondary antibody 30 min at room temperature, wash briefly, develop with CDP‑Star chemiluminescent substrate (Roche) for 15 min, and visualize with a CCD camera.

steps.title: Lumipulse immunoassay
steps.instruction: Start the Lumipulse G600II (Fujirebio). Load the appropriate cartridge for each marker (total tau, phospho‑tau‑181, Aβ42, Aβ40). Pipette 500 µl of the collected elution buffer into the Hitachi cup, place the cup in the rack, and run the automated assay. Results are available after 35 min; include standard curves and quality controls for verification.
